threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think Clapton is part of Hackney, not a whole other vibe. That and asking for directions instead of just sharing the pavement.
Last night on the 35, a guy pulled out a full chess set and started a game with a stranger. Only in Brixton, I swear.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The sound of an old lady yelling at her cat in the morning instead of church bells really hit home. This place has its own rhythm.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you spot a spontaneous outdoor gallery pop up on a street corner while sipping a late-night kebab. It's an art exhibit and snack bar all in one.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their disdain for BART's small talk—'mornings are for silence' is a common mantra, especially after delays.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a pigeon casually riding the 47 last week, just strutting down the aisle like it owned the place. Only in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's plazas are just for sipping sangria, but locals know they're really for kids playing futbol until sundown.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they still look up at the buildings instead of walking with their heads down, lost in their phones.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Tube' instead of the 'Overground' and get baffled when people assume you know the bus routes by heart.
Last night on the 196 bus, a guy sat across from me rummaged through a bag of fried chicken like it was gold. He offered me a wing like we were old mates.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a cat calmly perched on a bus stop sign, waiting for its owner who was busy chatting on the corner. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a corner café where every table has a board game. You can sip your coffee while rolling dice and claiming territories.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they weave through the BART delays without breaking a sweat, while newcomers stare at their phones confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a pigeon hitching a ride on the back of a Muni bus today. That bird looked like it owned the place—only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can see all the sights at a leisurely pace, but locals know rush hour means watching the clock, not the architecture.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their hesitation at ordering 'café con leche'—they always ask for 'just coffee' first.
